;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)]]
**A [[United States Armed Forces|U.S.]] [[airstrike]] kills an employee of the telecoms [[Hormuud Telecom]]. It was aimed at [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] in [[Jilib]], [[Middle Juba]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-security/somalia-telecoms-employee-killed-by-u-s-air-strike-company-idUSKBN20J26S?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**As fighting continues in the [[Idlib Governorate]], the [[Syrian Army]] takes control of rebel-stronghold [[Kafr Nabl|Kafranbel]] for the first time since 2012, and 18 nearby villages including [[Sheikh Dames]] and [[Sheikh Mustafa, Idlib|Sheikh Mustafa]]. [http://www.rfi.fr/en/wires/20200225-syrian-regime-retakes-symbolic-town-kafranbel-monitor (RFI)]
**[[Turkey|Turkish]]-backed rebels recapture the village of [[Nayrab, Idlib|Nayrab]], west of [[Saraqib]], after days of heavy fighting which has left dozens dead, according to Turkish state media. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/turkey-backed-fighters-recapture-key-town-syria-idlib-200225063927682.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Turkish military intervention in the Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] confirms the first [[Turkish Armed Forces]] casualties in [[Libya]] since beginning a military operation in support of the [[Government of National Accord|GNA]] government after two troops are killed. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-51626743 (BBC News)]
*[[North East Delhi riots]]
**Violent clashes in [[North East Delhi]], [[India]], between [[Hinduism in India|Hindu]] and [[Islam in India|Muslim]] protesters over the [[Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019|Citizenship Amendment Act]] continues leaving 13 people dead and at least 150 injured. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/pm-narendra-modi-tweets-appeal-to-my-sisters-and-brothers-of-delhi-to-maintain-peace-and-brotherhood-2185982 (NDTV)]

;Business and economy
*Steve Hasker, former [[President (corporate title)|company president]] of American data firm [[Nielsen Holdings]], is appointed CEO of [[Thomson Reuters]] effective March 15. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thomson-reuters-results/thomson-reuters-names-new-ceo-earnings-top-estimates-idUSKBN20J1LK?il=0 (Reuters)] [https://www.wsj.com/articles/thomson-reuters-names-former-nielsen-executive-as-ceo-11582636314 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*[[Bob Iger]] steps down as CEO of [[The Walt Disney Company]], and is succeeded by [[Bob Chapek]], former chairman of [[Disney Parks, Experiences and Products]]. Iger will continue to serve the company's "creative endeavors" as executive chairman. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-walt-disney-ceo-idUSKBN20J2NV (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
***93 more coronavirus cases are confirmed in [[Italy]], bringing the number to 322. Four more virus-related deaths are confirmed, bringing the death toll to eleven. [http://www.ansa.it/canale_saluteebenessere/notizie/sanita/2020/02/25/coronavirus-italia-_cd6f6294-4a0d-4645-b087-6cc2049ecfff.html (Agenzia ANSA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
***Two people from [[Lombardy]], [[Italy]], living in [[Austria]]'s state of [[Tyrol]], test positive for coronavirus. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2020/feb/25/coronavirus-live-updates-outbreak-latest-news-italy-italia-deaths-symptoms-china-stocks-wall-street-dow-jones-economy-falls?page=with:block-5e550afd8f086a28115b2205 (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]]
***[[Croatia]] confirms its first case of coronavirus. The patient had stayed in [[Milan]], Italy, from 19 to 21 February, and was hospitalised in [[Zagreb]], Croatia. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2020/feb/25/coronavirus-live-updates-outbreak-latest-news-italy-italia-deaths-symptoms-china-stocks-wall-street-dow-jones-economy-falls?page=with:block-5e550d8a8f086a28115b222d#block-5e550d8a8f086a28115b222d (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
***Iran's deputy health minister, Iraj Harirchi, tests positive for coronavirus. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/iran-deputy-health-minister-has-coronavirus-covid-19-adviser-12469574 (CNA)]
***A member of the [[Iranian Parliament]], [[Mahmoud Sadeghi]], states on [[Twitter]] that he has been infected with the virus. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/coronavirus-live-updates-irans-deputy-health-minister-tests-positive/ar-BB10lO9z?ocid=spartandhp (''New York Times'' via MSN News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
***Hundreds of guests are locked down in a hotel in [[Tenerife]], Spain, after a visiting Italian doctor tested positive for the virus. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51627597 (BBC News)]
***The first case on the peninsula and the fourth in the country is confirmed in [[Barcelona]], [[Catalonia]]. The wife of the Italian doctor becomes the fifth infected in Spain. A sixth case is reported in [[Villarreal]]. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/vida/20200225/473782485232/coronavirus-primer-caso-cataluna.html? (''La Vanguardia'')] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
***[[Switzerland]] confirms its first case of coronavirus: a case in [[Ticino]], on the border with [[Italy]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2020/feb/25/coronavirus-live-updates-outbreak-latest-news-italy-italia-deaths-symptoms-china-stocks-wall-street-dow-jones-economy-falls?page=with:block-5e550d8a8f086a28115b222d#block-5e550d8a8f086a28115b222d (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Algeria]] confirms its first case of the coronavirus. The patient is an Italian man who arrived in the country a week ago. [https://africatimes.com/2020/02/25/algerian-health-minister-confirms-first-covid-19-case/ (Africa Times)]
**[[Canada]]'s largest airline [[Air Canada]] suspends all flights to [[China]] until April in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/travel-coronavirus-champagne-advisories-1.5475003 (CBC)]

;International relations
*[[China–Sweden relations]]
**The [[Ministry for Foreign Affairs (Sweden)|Swedish Foreign Ministry]] summons the [[China|Chinese]] ambassador after the Chinese government sentences bookseller and [[Swedish nationality law|Swedish citizen]] [[Gui Minhai]] to ten years in prison for espionage. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-sweden-bookseller-diplomacy/sweden-summons-chinese-ambassador-to-demand-release-of-gui-minhai-idUSKBN20J1XE?il=0 (Reuters)] 

;Law and crime
*A man was revealed to have been arrested the previous day for attempting to blow up a car in [[The Pentagon]] parking lot. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/military/arkansas-man-tried-blow-suv-pentagon-parking-lot-feds-say-n1142611 (NBC)]
*Aimee Anne Duffy, a Welsh singer who goes by [[Duffy (singer)|Duffy]], reveals she was raped, drugged and held hostage over some days resulting in her disappearance from the limelight in recent years. [https://www.theguardian.com/music/2020/feb/25/pop-star-duffy-says-she-was-raped-drugged-and-held-captive (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Germany|German]] Health Minister [[Jens Spahn]] declines to run for leadership of the ruling [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|Christian Democratic Union]] party, and endorses [[North Rhine-Westphalia]] Minister-President [[Armin Laschet]] for the position. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-germany-politics-cdu/german-minister-spahn-out-of-race-to-lead-merkels-party-sources-idUSKCN20J0XH?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Saudi government]] appoints former [[Ministry of Energy (Saudi Arabia)|energy minister]] [[Khalid A. Al-Falih]] to head a new investment ministry replacing the [[Saudi Arabian General Investment Authority|General Investment Authority]], and sacks the [[Ministry of Media (Saudi Arabia)|media minister]], among other changes to the cabinet. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-cabinet/saudi-ex-energy-minister-bounces-back-as-investment-chief-idUSKBN20J232?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Former [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] leader [[David Steel]] resigns from the party and announces he will leave the [[House of Lords|UK House of Lords]] after a report accused him of “abdicat[ing] his responsibility” when he supported the knighthood of former [[Chief Whip of the Liberal Democrats|party whip]] [[Cyril Smith]], who is accused of child molestation. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/feb/25/lord-steel-quits-lib-dems-after-child-abuse-inquiry-report (''The Guardian'')]
